title: Are You…? Yes/No Questions with be
objective: Form and answer yes/no questions with be, using inversion and rising intonation.
intro_md: [L1: In this lesson you ask yes/no questions by moving am/is/are to the front: You are new. → Are you new? In these questions your voice goes UP at the end.]
notes: TODO_audio: ex2 (statement vs question pair, 1.0x), ex6 (Is your class in the morning?, 0.75x), ex8 speaking model prompt. Band map §15 allots L09 no new vocabulary (grammar G6 only); all question apparatus is function words, content words recycled from L01-L07. Band map also places a spoken guided-qa AI interaction at L09 — ex9 is that slot.

exercises.prompt: Are you…? · Is she…? · Am I…? · Yes, I am. · No, I'm not.
exercises.rationale: Inversion presented first as three audible question frames, paired with the L08 short answers they trigger — chunks before rule.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 1.0x] 'You're a student.' … 'Are you a student?' — [L1: Which one is the question?]
exercises.rationale: P3: question recognition from inversion plus rising melody at zero grammar cost — the perceptual foundation for everything else in the lesson.

options.label: Are you a student?
options.rationale: are moves to the front and the voice rises at the end — both signals mark the question.

options.label: You're a student.
options.rationale: Same words, statement order, falling voice: catches learners relying on words instead of order and melody.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Put the words in order to make a question.]
exercises.rationale: Inversion practice: zh/vi (and informal es) form questions by intonation alone, so the predicted answer is statement order 'You are from Mexico?' — feedback names the fronted are.
Agreement must survive inversion (is with she); She's in the bank catches learners who keep statement order and only add a question mark.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match each question to its short answer.]
exercises.rationale: Person-switching between question and answer (you→I, he→he, they→they) is where learners break; pairs cover singular, plural and negative in one screen.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'Is your class in the morning?' — [L1: Choose the correct answer.]
exercises.rationale: Short answers with it for a thing (your class) — learners default to repeating the noun or dropping the pronoun; also recycles L01 morning in a new frame.

options.label: Yes, it is.
options.rationale: it stands for your class; is echoes the question's be-form — pronoun plus full form.

options.label: Yes, is.
options.rationale: Pronoun drop (es 'Sí, es'): English short answers always need the subject pronoun.

options.label: Yes, it's.
options.rationale: Sentence-final contraction — recycles the L08 trap in the new it-frame to check the rule generalized.

exercises.rationale: Spanish questions need no inversion and no article ('¿Eres estudiante?'); the English version forces both changes at once — fronted are and a before the noun.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Ask the AI if it is from your country. Start with Are, and make your voice go up at the end.]
asr_focus: rising final contour (P3 — flat or falling melody flagged)
are produced before you (no intonation-only question)
exercises.rationale: Produces inversion and the rising contour together; ASR flags the intonation-only question that zh/vi/es speakers transfer.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Guessing game. The AI is thinking of a country you know and of what it is (student or teacher). Ask only yes/no questions with Are you / Is it, then guess.]
exercises.rationale: Information-checking is the band-file communicative need for G6; a guessing game makes inversion the tool, not the topic. Fills the L09 spoken guided-qa AI slot from band map §15.
